title: electrolyteActivity operation
description: Mean-ionic activity and osmotic coefficients of the salt the CASE's declared thermophysical system carries — the package's own electrolyte surface, exercised directly. Where `pitzerActivity` names its salt by two ions and is the model's bench, this op takes the salt from the declaration and is the PACKAGE's bench: the numbers here are exactly what the flowsheet units will see, which is the point of running it before them.

molality.title: Molality scan
molality.description: `{ from ...; to ...; n ...; }` — the molality range to sweep.

output.title: CSV output
output.description: `{ file <name>.csv; }` — where the per-row results are written, relative to the case directory.

table.title: Design table (mass fraction x temperature)
table.description: `{ massFractions ( ... ); temperatures ( ... ); file <name>.csv; }` (or `molalities ( ... )` in place of `massFractions`) — for each point: molality, a_w, the boiling-point rise at that temperature as the boiling temperature, EXACT (a_w Psat(T) = Psat(T − BPE), the evaporator's own relation) and LINEARISED (−R T²/ΔHvap · ln a_w), L_phi, the solution enthalpy on the chart datum (liquid water at 0 °C, the salt at infinite dilution at 20 °C) and, for a model built from separate activity and enthalpy correlations, its Gibbs-Helmholtz gap. Diagnostics aw_/BPE_exact_/BPE_linear_/Lphi_/Hchart_/GHgap_ tagged _w<wt%>_T<°C> (or _m<m>_T<°C>).
